newsitem.title: USA: Clinton request may affect News and Echo.
newsitem.headline: Clinton request may affect News and Echo.

text.p: The Clinton administration on Monday asked regulators to delay ruling on whether MCI Communications Corp can transfer its valuable satellite-TV license to British Telecommunications Plc under the companies' proposed merger.

In a letter to Federal Communications Commission Chairman Reed Hundt, the administration asked the FCC first to issue rules governing foreign ownership of a U.S. satellite-TV service before ruling on the license transfer.

"We believe that significant policy questions continue to exist regarding foreign-ownership of (direct broadcast satellite) services on U.S. licensed satellites," said the letter, which was signed by senior officials at the Commerce Department, the State Department and the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative.

The letter recommended that the FCC fully review the issue "before reaching a final determination on any applications that involve foreign ownership above the statutory levels applicable to common carrier or broadcast licenses."

The administration also urged the FCC to formulate and issue rules promptly "on whether and how foreign ownership restrictions and public interest criteria should be applied to subscription DBS services on U.S.-licensed satellites, prior to reaching a final determination on any application that may be affected by the outcome of the rulemaking."

Attornies said any rulemaking could pose a problem for BT and MCI. It also could affect Rupert Murdoch's bid to take a $1 billion stake in EchoStar Communications Corp, although that deal is in danger of unraveling for other reasons.
But Scott Harris, an attorney for Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher, said he saw only limited impact on the BT-MCI deal.

"It is inconceivable that the administration letter will slow down consideration of the BT-MCI transaction. Nobody either in the administration or at the commission would attempt to hold hostage a transaction of this importance to an open-ended review of satellite policy," said Harris, the former head of the FCC's international bureau.

"In all likelihood, the commiission will approve the BT-MCI transaction late this summer or early next fall and make it conditional on any change in its foreign-ownership rules on DBS satellites," said Harris.
But he added: "Those rules are not likely to be changed."
